I’m moving the request into leaf components behind close Suspense boundaries and giving each boundary a layout-shaped fallback, so the title, card labels, section headings, and placeholders all ship in the prerendered shell while the data remains fresh per request.

item.text:
Optimized the PPR shell.

- [page.tsx](/workspace/app/page.tsx:46) is now synchronous, so the dashboard heading and structure prerender immediately.
- Each data section has a close Suspense boundary with a layout-matched skeleton. Identical GET requests are memoized during the render, avoiding duplicate network calls. [Next.js recommends this pattern](https://nextjs.org/docs/app/getting-started/partial-prerendering).
- [loading.tsx](/workspace/app/loading.tsx:5) now reuses the full dashboard shell instead of showing only a spinner.
- Added typed response data and HTTP error handling.

Verification:

- `npm run build` passes; `/` remains `◐` Partial Prerender.
- Generated HTML now contains `Dashboard`, both stat labels, `Revenue`, and `Latest Invoices`; previously it contained only the loading spinner.
- `npx tsc --noEmit` and `git diff --check` pass.

The existing `api.example.com` placeholder still needs a real endpoint for streamed runtime data. Pre-existing `package.json` and lockfile changes were left untouched.
